title: Daily UTC delivery lateness CSV report
brief: Design a small daily report that joins two CSV files by order ID. One has promised-delivery timestamps and the other actual-delivery timestamps, both ISO UTC. Flag delivered orders more than 24 hours late and export a CSV for the operations team. No emails, remote updates, forecasting or conversational interface.

assumptions.statement: The proposed CSV contract is UTF-8 with optional BOM, comma delimiter and one header; promised columns are order_id,promised_delivery_utc and actual columns are order_id,actual_delivery_utc. Extra columns are ignored. IDs are case-sensitive ASCII [A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_-]{0,63}, unique within each file; empty or padded IDs are errors.
assumptions.why: Exact schemas and an ID profile were not supplied; strict validation avoids accidental joins and spreadsheet formula execution.
assumptions.validation: Inspect representative exports, including leading-zero IDs and unusual ID characters; approve this contract or version a replacement before launch.

assumptions.statement: Operations supplies two complete snapshots from the same order namespace and consistent export cutoff after the requested day ends. CSVs have no authoritative dataset/as-of metadata; the job cannot independently prove their business freshness or shared provenance.
assumptions.why: A correct join can still be wrong when files come from different sources or omit recently recorded deliveries.
assumptions.validation: Verify export procedure and late-arrival/correction timing; record source, cutoff and pair-selection evidence in the operating runbook before use.

assumptions.statement: The daily report covers actual deliveries in the previous UTC calendar day by default, with an explicit --report-date override for backfills. It contains all delivered rows in that day, not only late rows; a boolean identifies lateness.
assumptions.why: Daily window and output inclusion were unspecified. One row per delivered order supports reconciliation and shows on-time results.
assumptions.validation: Confirm daily window and all-deliveries output on representative manual examples before launch.

assumptions.statement: Accepted timestamps use YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS[.ffffff]Z or +00:00, with 1-6 fractional digits, valid Gregorian dates and seconds 00-59. Empty actual means undelivered; non-UTC offsets, missing promised values, leap seconds and greater precision fail validation.
assumptions.why: ISO UTC is broader than a single parser profile; exact bounded precision gives deterministic arithmetic.
assumptions.validation: Check real timestamp samples and establish this profile; unsupported valid ISO forms require an explicit parser-contract revision.

assumptions.statement: Proposed operational budget is at most 100,000 rows and 50 MiB per file, 120 seconds per run, and a once-daily invocation at 08:00 UTC after exports are ready. Operations reviews local status by 10:00 UTC and acknowledges failures by 12:00 UTC; after that the operations lead manually escalates.
assumptions.why: Small, daily and operations ownership need concrete provisional limits and a local failure disposition.
assumptions.validation: Measure actual sizes/runtime and confirm schedule, staffing, acknowledgement and escalation practice before launch; tune versioned limits if necessary.

assumptions.statement: Run on one trusted local host/account with two allowlisted input roots, a dedicated output root and same-filesystem staging. Only the job may mutate its output root; no symlinks are permitted in resolved input/output paths. An operator grants these local capabilities in configuration.
assumptions.why: Local filesystem isolation and atomic-directory publication are proposed controls, not verified deployment facts.
assumptions.validation: Exercise permissions, exclusive locks, fsync and directory rename/crash behavior on the chosen filesystem; confirm trusted-account boundary.

assumptions.statement: Keep committed CSVs, manifests and local failure records for 30 days. Do not copy raw input files; persist hashes, counts and error row numbers without row contents. Delete expired files locally only through a separate operator-maintained procedure.
assumptions.why: No retention policy or personal-data classification was supplied; minimization and a provisional retention period need approval.
assumptions.validation: Approve access, retention and order-ID sensitivity before launch; verify any stricter organizational requirement.

assumptions.statement: A date with an existing valid completed report is immutable: identical input/config returns ALREADY_COMPLETE; changed input/config returns CONFLICT. Corrections require the owner to archive the old date directory outside this job and rerun; no replacement action is implemented.
assumptions.why: Silent overwrites can cause the operations team to act on inconsistent reports.
assumptions.validation: Approve the manual correction/runbook rule and prove conflict behavior in a local staging environment.

items.title: Business decision and actors
items.description: Operations uses the exported daily CSV to identify which delivered orders exceeded their promised delivery timestamp by strictly more than 24 hours. The tool reports facts; it does not decide compensation, contact customers or change orders. Proposed owner roles are not named people or confirmed appointments.
items.reasoning: A bounded report should make the operations decision and data contract reviewable.

items.title: Date and data rules
items.description: Validate entire snapshots before filtering. Blank actual timestamps are undelivered and excluded. A delivered actual ID with no promised row fails the run, even outside the report window; promised-only rows are counted as undelivered/not matched. Duplicate IDs in either file fail the entire run even if rows are identical. Only actual rows within [D 00:00:00Z,(D+1) 00:00:00Z) are reported. Signed lateness uses exact integer microseconds: flag iff actual-promised > 86400000000. Actual before promised is valid and not late. Empty values, bad headers/CSV/UTF-8, duplicate header names, invalid timestamps, non-UTC values and unsafe IDs block publication.

sources.passage: Design a small daily report that joins two CSV files by order ID. One has promised-delivery timestamps and the other actual-delivery timestamps, both ISO UTC. Flag delivered orders more than 24 hours late and export a CSV for the operations team. No emails, remote updates, forecasting or conversational interface.

The proposed CSV contract is UTF-8 with optional BOM, comma delimiter and one header; promised columns are order_id,promised_delivery_utc and actual columns are order_id,actual_delivery_utc. Extra columns are ignored. IDs are case-sensitive ASCII [A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_-]{0,63}, unique within each file; empty or padded IDs are errors.

Operations supplies two complete snapshots from the same order namespace and consistent export cutoff after the requested day ends. CSVs have no authoritative dataset/as-of metadata; the job cannot independently prove their business freshness or shared provenance.

Proposed operational budget is at most 100,000 rows and 50 MiB per file, 120 seconds per run, and a once-daily invocation at 08:00 UTC after exports are ready. Operations reviews local status by 10:00 UTC and acknowledges failures by 12:00 UTC; after that the operations lead manually escalates.

Run on one trusted local host/account with two allowlisted input roots, a dedicated output root and same-filesystem staging. Only the job may mutate its output root; no symlinks are permitted in resolved input/output paths. An operator grants these local capabilities in configuration.

Keep committed CSVs, manifests and local failure records for 30 days. Do not copy raw input files; persist hashes, counts and error row numbers without row contents. Delete expired files locally only through a separate operator-maintained procedure.

A date with an existing valid completed report is immutable: identical input/config returns ALREADY_COMPLETE; changed input/config returns CONFLICT. Corrections require the owner to archive the old date directory outside this job and rerun; no replacement action is implemented.

sources.passage: Design a small daily report that joins two CSV files by order ID. One has promised-delivery timestamps and the other actual-delivery timestamps, both ISO UTC. Flag delivered orders more than 24 hours late and export a CSV for the operations team. No emails, remote updates, forecasting or conversational interface.

The proposed CSV contract is UTF-8 with optional BOM, comma delimiter and one header; promised columns are order_id,promised_delivery_utc and actual columns are order_id,actual_delivery_utc. Extra columns are ignored. IDs are case-sensitive ASCII [A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_-]{0,63}, unique within each file; empty or padded IDs are errors.

The daily report covers actual deliveries in the previous UTC calendar day by default, with an explicit --report-date override for backfills. It contains all delivered rows in that day, not only late rows; a boolean identifies lateness.

Accepted timestamps use YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS[.ffffff]Z or +00:00, with 1-6 fractional digits, valid Gregorian dates and seconds 00-59. Empty actual means undelivered; non-UTC offsets, missing promised values, leap seconds and greater precision fail validation.

Proposed operational budget is at most 100,000 rows and 50 MiB per file, 120 seconds per run, and a once-daily invocation at 08:00 UTC after exports are ready. Operations reviews local status by 10:00 UTC and acknowledges failures by 12:00 UTC; after that the operations lead manually escalates.

Run on one trusted local host/account with two allowlisted input roots, a dedicated output root and same-filesystem staging. Only the job may mutate its output root; no symlinks are permitted in resolved input/output paths. An operator grants these local capabilities in configuration.

A date with an existing valid completed report is immutable: identical input/config returns ALREADY_COMPLETE; changed input/config returns CONFLICT. Corrections require the owner to archive the old date directory outside this job and rerun; no replacement action is implemented.

sources.passage: Design a small daily report that joins two CSV files by order ID. One has promised-delivery timestamps and the other actual-delivery timestamps, both ISO UTC. Flag delivered orders more than 24 hours late and export a CSV for the operations team. No emails, remote updates, forecasting or conversational interface.

The proposed CSV contract is UTF-8 with optional BOM, comma delimiter and one header; promised columns are order_id,promised_delivery_utc and actual columns are order_id,actual_delivery_utc. Extra columns are ignored. IDs are case-sensitive ASCII [A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_-]{0,63}, unique within each file; empty or padded IDs are errors.

The daily report covers actual deliveries in the previous UTC calendar day by default, with an explicit --report-date override for backfills. It contains all delivered rows in that day, not only late rows; a boolean identifies lateness.

Accepted timestamps use YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS[.ffffff]Z or +00:00, with 1-6 fractional digits, valid Gregorian dates and seconds 00-59. Empty actual means undelivered; non-UTC offsets, missing promised values, leap seconds and greater precision fail validation.

Proposed operational budget is at most 100,000 rows and 50 MiB per file, 120 seconds per run, and a once-daily invocation at 08:00 UTC after exports are ready. Operations reviews local status by 10:00 UTC and acknowledges failures by 12:00 UTC; after that the operations lead manually escalates.

Run on one trusted local host/account with two allowlisted input roots, a dedicated output root and same-filesystem staging. Only the job may mutate its output root; no symlinks are permitted in resolved input/output paths. An operator grants these local capabilities in configuration.

A date with an existing valid completed report is immutable: identical input/config returns ALREADY_COMPLETE; changed input/config returns CONFLICT. Corrections require the owner to archive the old date directory outside this job and rerun; no replacement action is implemented.
